blogs.title: The Silent Desaturation: When 'Ondine's Curse' Isn't Congenital
blogs.description: This post explores the fascinating pathophysiology of acquired central hypoventilation in Chiari Malformation Type I (CMI). It analyzes the dissociation between voluntary and automatic breathing control, explaining why patients can maintain normal ventilation while awake but suffer life-threatening hypoxia during sleep or distraction without sensing dyspnea. We will discuss the clinical red flags of asymptomatic desaturation (SpO2 70-80%) and why a high index of suspicion for brainstem compression is required when pulmonary workups are unrevealing.

blogs.title: Choking on Nothing: The Neurogenic Dysphagia Blind Spot
blogs.description: Focusing on the diagnostic odyssey of the patient's 7-year history of choking, this article argues for earlier neurological evaluation in cases of 'unexplained' dysphagia. We will contrast mechanical vs. neurogenic swallowing difficulties (solids AND liquids equally affected) and review the literature suggesting CMI prevalence is significantly higher in cohorts with persistent dysphagia than in the general population. The post serves as a reminder that normal ENT and GI scopes do not rule out a catastrophic brainstem etiology.

blogs.title: The 14-Year Miss: Re-Reading Trauma Scans for Crowded Foramen Magnum
blogs.description: A critical look at radiologic vigilance, this post details how a 'normal' CT scan performed 14 years prior actually contained the key to the diagnosis: a crowded foramen magnum. We will discuss the challenges of identifying CMI on non-contrast CT versus MRI, the concept of secondary/acquired Chiari following head trauma, and the medicolegal and clinical imperative to re-review historical imaging when faced with progressive, unexplained neurological decline.

blogs.title: Beyond the Valsalva Headache: Atypical Pain Presentations in Chiari I
blogs.description: While occipital headaches worsened by Valsalva are the hallmark of Chiari Syndrome, this case presented with unique vertex allodynia and 'burning vertex' symptoms relieved only by cutting hair. This post examines under-recognized pain phenotypes associated with CMI, including occipital neuralgia and cutaneous allodynia. It challenges clinicians to broaden their differential for chronic scalp pain and headache syndromes that don't fit classic migraine or tension-type profiles.

blogs.title: The AHI Trap: Why Standard Sleep Studies Underestimate Brainstem Apnea
blogs.description: This technical deep-dive addresses the discrepancy between severe clinical hypoxia and a deceptively mild Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) in CMI patients. We will explain how Type III sleep studies (lacking EEG) calculate AHI based on total recording time rather than true sleep time, leading to significant underestimation of central event frequency. The post advocates for comprehensive Type I polysomnography with capnography for any patient with suspected central hypoventilation syndromes.
